call_points.text: **Middle East outlook:** Softness is expected to continue across Q1 and part of Q2 FY27 due to the West Asia conflict disruptions.
**Component shortage:** Gaps in PC, smartphone, and GPU supply will drive revenue fulfillment for the next 12 to 18 months.
**Large deals scale:** Large deal executions totaled over ₹2,500 Cr in FY26, with pipeline momentum expected to increase in H1FY27.
**Working capital:** Working capital days reduced to 30 days in Q4, but could increase due to component buffer stocking and larger deals.
**Arena losses:** Turkey subsidiary Arena is expected to remain loss-making in FY27 at a reduced level, turning profitable in FY28.
**SSG margins:** Software Solutions Group tracks around 5.5% gross margin, with intent to maintain between 5.5% and 6.0%.
**Capital allocation:** Retained cash will support potential inorganic professional services acquisitions in cloud and cybersecurity.

operating_notes.text: SISA segment FY26 revenue ₹65,033 Cr vs ROW ₹54,182 Cr; SISA Q4 PBT ₹412 Cr vs ROW loss of ₹16.78 Cr after impairment.
Arena Bilgisayar (Turkey) trade-name impairment of ₹152.31 Cr recognised in Q4FY26 on challenging Turkey economic conditions.
Redington International Mauritius re-domiciled to UAE; Redington Kenya (EPZ) dissolved effective January 28, 2026.
Large deal execution reached over ₹1,100 Cr in TSG in Q4FY26 and ~₹2,500 Cr across FY26.
Working capital days stood at 30 days as of Q4FY26.
SSG recurring revenue was 74% of FY26 revenue (72% in FY25), with a renewal rate of about 85% and banked revenue for next year at 63.5%.
Top six vendors (Microsoft, AWS, Autodesk, Red Hat, Fortinet, Palo Alto) contribute over 70% of SSG revenue; SSG works with 130-plus brands across 40-plus markets.
SSG revenue recognition under IFRS leaves about a 5% gap between invoiced gross revenue and reported revenue; FY26 invoiced revenue was about $150 million above the $2.2 billion reported.
Channel holds about 2-3 months of inventory, mainly in Endpoint Solutions stock-and-sell; PC prices rose 25-50% over 2-3 quarters with single-digit unit growth.
Data-centre large deals of nearly ₹1,000 Cr in Q1FY27, about ₹700 Cr from India, with a backlog several times that for the next few quarters.
Arena debt fell to $90 million from $120-130 million; Q1 interest cost including factoring fell to ₹37 Cr from ₹69 Cr.
Redington Gulf holds six AWS Competencies, including AWS AI Services and AWS Digital Sovereignty Services Competency, and will distribute AWS alongside other AWS Partner Network members in META.
